1	# Spike DEVDESK-198: Charm v2 migration (Bubble Tea, Bubbles, Lip Gloss, ntcharts)
2	
3	2026-11-10, Linux, Go 1.27.3. Base: `origin/main` at 63ebd72 (DEVDESK-197, 199, 200 merged).
4	Experiment code: branch `spike/charm-v2-code` (commit 217b389), **to be discarded, never merged**. This report is the only deliverable.
5	Pinned versions (not reopened): `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` v2.1.1, `charm.land/bubbles/v2` v2.2.1, `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` v2.0.6, `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` v0.11.9, `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` v2.9.0 (exact module path confirmed with `go list -m`; its `go.mod` requires bubbletea v2.1.1 and lipgloss v2.0.6, no `replace`). `go mod tidy` also pulled `go-runewidth` v0.0.16 to v0.0.31 and `colorprofile` v0.4.3.
6	
7	Method: sed the imports, let the compiler lead, fix by category. The spike ended **with everything compiling and `go test ./...` green** (run once, `-timeout 100s`; `go vet ./...` clean). The only deleted tests are the three of `internal/ui/testutil` (`keys_test.go`, `source_guard_test.go`, `testutil_test.go`) and `colorprofile_test.go`, which test v1 APIs and are to be rewritten (see criteria 4 and 5). Not run: `mise run lint`, `test-race` (needs cgo), the app in a real terminal.
8	
9	## Summary
10	
11	| # | Criterion | Verdict | One line |
12	|---|---|---|---|
13	| 1 | Imports on theme, datatable, about | OK | Mechanical. datatable: 0 production line beyond imports; theme: 4 logic spots; about: 1 method. The plan's counts hold, with two corrections (`termenv`, tests) |
14	| 2 | Palette `color.Color` | OK with reserve | 91 type sites, 3 logic spots; Rule 119 holds; **`lipgloss.Color("")` is `NoColor` whose `RGBA()` is opaque black** and an invalid hex is silently `NoColor` |
15	| 3 | `Render()` + `View() tea.View` + `Screen` | OK | Compiles, **0 `handle*` signature changed** (271 of them, 429 `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)` returns). Cost: 14 `.(Screen)` assertions in the router, tests renamed to `Render()` |
16	| 4 | Colour profile | OK with reserve | `tea.WithColorProfile` verified on a real `tea.Program`. 13 test files with termenv was really 3; **7 tests silently depended on the Ascii profile** |
17	| 5 | `testutil.Msgs` and `tea.Sequence` | OK | Reflection works unchanged: `sequenceMsg` is still `[]tea.Cmd` |
18	| 6 | ntcharts v2 sparkline | OK | One import line changed; `WithStyle(lipgloss.Style)` (v2); dashboard tests green |
19	| 7 | Rules 125 / 116, runewidth vs engine | OK with reserve | Layout byte-identical to v1 at 3 sizes. The engine's width depends on terminal mode 2027: **cannot be verified without a real terminal** |
20	| 8 | Viewport keys, `PasteMsg` | OK with reserve | Viewport: no change needed. **Paste is lost by the router and by every `KeyMsg`-gated field** (fixed in the router and `FilterBar`; ~34 sites remain to audit) |
21	| 9 | Commit split and effort | OK, adjusted | Same seven commits, reordered into compilable-in-the-end groups; effort L confirmed (2 to 3 days of coding, plus manual terminal checks) |
22	
23	## 1. Imports on theme, datatable, about
24	
25	Counts on `main` (import lines), against §1 of `charm-v2-impact.md`:
26	
27	| Import | Plan | Measured |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| bubbletea | 239 files | 261 files (tests included) |
30	| lipgloss | 147 | 151 |
31	| bubbles spinner / textinput / table / viewport / key | 39 / 26 / 21 / 6 / 1 | 39 / 26 / 21 / 6 / 1 (identical) |
32	| x/ansi | 52 `ansi.*` | 53 imports |
33	| `termenv` | 13 test files | **3 files** (DEVDESK-199 funnelled it into `internal/testutil/colorprofile`; 50 callers of that helper stay unchanged) |
34	
35	One `sed` over the whole repo (376 files) replaced them. Also needed: two `string`-literal fixes, because the sed hit import paths quoted in two guard tests.
36	
37	What compiles and what breaks, per package, after the import swap only:
38	
39	| Package | Production code | Tests |
40	|---|---|---|
41	| `theme` | `colors.go`: 76 declarations `lipgloss.Color` to `color.Color` (type, mechanical). 15 more type sites elsewhere. `contrast.go`, `tokencolors.go` (read hex from the string): rewritten. `StyleTextInput` (textinput styles): rewritten. `manager.go`: **0 change** (`lipgloss.Color(hex)` is now a function and still compiles) | 72 compile errors in 13 files: 37 string constants given as `color.Color`, ~12 `string(c)`, 8 `lipgloss.TerminalColor`, rest `string` literals. Fixed with a 40-line script (wrap in `lipgloss.Color(...)`, `string(c)` to `theme.Hex(c)`). 1 failing test: the SGR reset is now `\x1b[m`, not `\x1b[0m` |
42	| `datatable` | **0 line** (builds as is, it does not use `bubbles/table` rendering) | compiles after `testutil` is ported; 4 tests fail until 8 literals `"\x1b[0m"` become `"\x1b[m"` |
43	| `about` | `View() string` becomes `Render() string` plus a 1-line `View() tea.View` | 3 `.View()` to `.Render()`; 1 test (see criterion 4) |
44	| `components` (dependency) | 2 sites `textinput.Width = n` to `SetWidth(n)` (23 such sites repo-wide) | 14 lines |
45	
46	Whole repo, production code: 209 files, +747 / -623. Tests: 203 files, +1070 / -1585 (the deletions are the four removed test files). The compiler found everything except the five silent points listed in criteria 2, 4, 8 and below.
47	
48	**Silent points actually hit** (compiler-silent, caught by tests): the space key (`keymap.Space` is `" "` in v1; flipping that one constant to `"space"` took the failures from about 50 to 11, which is the DEVDESK-200 payoff); the paste (criterion 8); the SGR reset `\x1b[m` (9 literals in 6 test files: 8 in datatable, 1 regexp in theme; `overlay.go` already accepts both); 7 tests that assumed no ANSI (criterion 4).
49	
50	Mechanical changes beyond imports, with site counts: `WithWhitespaceBackground` to `WithWhitespaceStyle(NewStyle().Background(c))` 16 sites (exact match with the plan); `textinput` `.Width` 23; textinput style assignments 3 (`theme.StyleTextInput`, `setup/styles.go`, `paletteInputView`); viewport `New(w,h)` 4, `.Width/.Height/.YOffset` reads and writes about 50 (including tests); `tea.WithAltScreen` 2 (now `View.AltScreen`). `bubbles/table` and `spinner` needed **no** change. `tea.KeyMsg` stays compilable (it is now an interface matching press and release): 103 production sites still use it; it works but should become `tea.KeyPressMsg` (release events only exist with keyboard enhancements, which we do not request).
51	
52	## 2. Palette
53	
54	Port (what I did): every `var Color… lipgloss.Color` becomes `color.Color` (`import "image/color"`). Semantic aliases (`ColorTableLineSelected`, `ColorSyntax*`, `ColorFooter*`, `IconColor`, `TokenColor`, `indicator.Color`, `cmdsuggest.Fg/Bg`) carry the same `color.Color`; an alias is an assignment, so `ApplyTheme` is unchanged.
55	
56	**Rule 119** (hex only in `colors.go`): holds. `colors.go` only declares; the hex strings live in `manager.go`'s `DefaultTheme` and theme files, and `ApplyTheme` calls `lipgloss.Color(hexString)` exactly as before. A grep for `#rrggbb` literals outside `manager.go`/`colors.go` finds comments only. The one addition is `theme.Hex(c color.Color) string` (formats `#rrggbb` or `none`), used by tests in place of `string(c)`; it produces hex, it does not hold any.
57	
58	`contrast.go` reads components through `RGBA()` (`uint32`, 16-bit, shift by 8), after a type check:
59	
60	```go
61	if _, ok := c.(color.RGBA); !ok { return error }   // only "#rgb"/"#rrggbb" come out as color.RGBA
62	r, g, b, _ := c.RGBA()
63	```
64	
65	Without the type check the old contract ("hex only, else error") is lost, because of the empty-colour semantics below. `TestContrast*`, `ColorDistance` pass; their "error" table (`"", "red", "12", "ffffff", "#ggg"...`) still errors, now because those values become `NoColor` or `ansi.BasicColor`.
66	
67	**Empty colour** (`iconcolors.go`, measured):
68	
69	| Input | v2 type | `RGBA()` | `Render` |
70	|---|---|---|---|
71	| `lipgloss.Color("")` | `lipgloss.NoColor` | **0 0 0 65535 (opaque black)** | no SGR emitted ("inherits", same effect as v1) |
72	| `Color("red")`, `Color("#ggg")` | `NoColor` (silently) | opaque black | none |
73	| `Color("#fff")` | `color.RGBA` | ok | 38;2 |
74	| `Color("12")` | `ansi.BasicColor` | palette | 38;5/ANSI |
75	| `NewStyle().GetForeground()` (unset) | `NoColor{}`, `== Color("")` is true | | |
76	
77	Consequences: (a) the rendering semantics of "no colour" are preserved, so the `IconColor` rule (unknown role falls back to `ColorText`, never the zero Color) still protects Rule 122 and `IconColor("nope") == ColorText` passes; (b) **anything reading components must type-check first**, because `NoColor.RGBA()` is black; (c) `app_header.go:190` (`GetForeground() != lipgloss.Color("")`) keeps working through interface equality; (d) **a typo in a theme hex is now silently no colour**, where `lipgloss.Color` kept the string; if `ApplyTheme` should reject it, validate at load (not done in the spike, flagged as a risk). Reserve: the `textinput` virtual cursor style is `NewStyle().Foreground(Cursor.Color)` only, so the cursor cell loses the old `Background(ColorBackground)` (Rule 115); visual check needed.
78	
79	## 3. Architecture: `Render() string` + `View() tea.View` + `Screen`
80	
81	Done as decided:
82	
83	```go
84	// each of the 17 views
85	func (m Model) Render() string { ... }                         // was View() string
86	func (m Model) View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }
87	
88	// router
89	type Screen interface { tea.Model; Render() string }
90	views map[command.ViewType]Screen
91	func (a *App) View() tea.View { v := tea.NewView(a.Render()); v.AltScreen = true; return v }
92	```
93	
94	`main.go` loses `tea.WithAltScreen()`; the setup wizard (its own root program) sets `AltScreen` in its own `View`.
95	
96	Result: **compiles, and no `handle*` signature changed.** `grep` finds 271 `handle*(...) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)` and 429 `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)` returns in production code (the plan said ~480); the diff touches none of them (the only added one is `handlePasteMsg`). Reason: `tea.Model` is still satisfied by the view.
97	
98	What it costs:
99	- 17 views: 17 renames + 17 one-line wrappers (scripted).
100	- Router: `Update` of a view returns `tea.Model`, so every `a.views[x] = updated` needs `updated.(Screen)`: **14 sites** in `internal/app` (it panics if a view stops implementing `Render`). A helper `a.setView(name, tea.Model)` would centralise it; I did not.
101	- 5 fake views in `internal/app/*_test.go` (+2 program wrappers): rename plus wrapper; `router()`, `routerAt()`, `commanding()` take a `Screen`.
102	- Tests: `.View()` on a view model becomes `.Render()`. 450 `.View()` calls in 104 test files; a script renamed all in the 17 view packages and `internal/app`, then reverted the 115 that were components (`datatable`, `FilterBar`, forms, which keep `View() string`). Tests may equally call `View().Content` (a `string` field, set by `NewView`); `Render()` is shorter and does not allocate a `tea.View`. Recommendation: `Render()` in tests.
103	- Components (`datatable`, `components.*`, `status/components`) keep `View() string`, as planned. Guards keyed on the method name `View` do not exist (`grep '"View"'` finds one test map), so the AST guards (`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody`, footer guards) are unaffected by the rename.
104	
105	## 4. Colour profile
106	
107	`lipgloss.SetColorProfile` is gone; `Style.Render` now always emits full colour (`\x1b[38;2;r;g;bm`). `internal/testutil/colorprofile` therefore keeps its API (`TrueColor(t)`, `Force()`) as **no-ops** (50 callers untouched) and its own test file is deleted; `termenv` leaves `go.mod`. `source_guard_test.go` still needs the same rule re-aimed ("no import of `colorprofile` other than the helper, no hand-built `tea.KeyPressMsg{}`").
108	
109	Replacement validated on a real `tea.Program` (`internal/app/spike_profile_test.go`, 3 cases, output captured in a buffer):
110	
111	| `tea.WithColorProfile(...)` | `38;2;` | `38;5;` | `38;` | alt screen `\x1b[?1049h` | bytes |
112	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
113	| TrueColor | yes | | | yes | 3499 |
114	| ANSI256 | no | yes | | yes | 2634 |
115	| Ascii | no | no | no | yes | 1402 |
116	
117	So downsampling happens at the output, and `View.AltScreen` replaces the program option. `ColorProfileMsg` is sent by the program after capability detection; the `main.go` `COLORTERM`/`WT_SESSION` workaround can become `tea.WithColorProfile(colorprofile.TrueColor)` when `WT_SESSION` is set (not changed in the spike; WSL/Windows Terminal not verified).
118	
119	Guards:
120	- `TestNoViewStylesItsOwnFooterMessage`: AST scan of function names containing `RenderFooter`/`InfoLine`/`InfoText`; passes unchanged, keeps its meaning.
121	- `TestNoPackageLevelVarRendersAString`: passes unchanged. Its doc comment lists two causes; **cause 2 (lipgloss `sync.Once` locking the profile at init) no longer exists**, cause 1 (string frozen on the default theme) remains and is enough to keep the test. Update the comment.
122	- datatable tests: all pass after the eight `\x1b[0m` literals. The Rule 116 tests (`TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth`) pass with x/ansi v0.11.9.
123	- **Hidden dependency found**: 7 tests asserted "blank line" or "empty info line" on raw `Render()` output and passed only because `go test` had no TTY, hence the Ascii profile (`about_test.go` says so in a comment: "under `go test` lipgloss finds no TTY and emits none"). In v2 the same line is `ESC[38;2;…m   ESC[m`. Fixed with `ansi.Strip` in `about`, `configuration`, `dashboard`, `netdiag`, `oci_resources`, `security` (x2). These tests did not check what they claimed to; `ansi.Strip` is the right form.
124	
125	## 5. `testutil.Msgs` and `tea.Sequence`
126	
127	Works unchanged. bubbletea v2.1.1 still has `type sequenceMsg []Cmd` (unexported) and `type BatchMsg []Cmd` (exported); the reflection (`Kind()==Slice && Elem()==TypeFor[tea.Cmd]()`) matches as before. Tested: `Msgs(tea.Sequence(c(1), tea.Batch(c(2), c(3)), c(4)))` returns the four messages in order. No replacement needed. Risk to note: this relies on the type staying a `[]Cmd`; `internal/ui/testutil` should keep the test that fails if bubbletea changes it.
128	
129	Other `testutil` changes (one 60-line file rewritten, all of `Key`/`Type`/`Paste`/`IsText`/`Text`): `Key` returns `tea.KeyPressMsg{Code, Text, Mod}`; space is `{Code: KeySpace, Text: " "}` (its `String()` is `"space"`); `alt+x` must clear `Text` (otherwise `String()` returns `x`, found by a test); `shift+tab` is `{Code: KeyTab, Mod: ModShift}`; `Paste` is `tea.PasteMsg{Content}`. The 1295 `testutil.Key` call sites needed no change; 22 tests that name `tea.KeyMsg` kept compiling.
130	
131	## 6. ntcharts v2 sparkline
132	
133	OK. `internal/ui/dashboard/chart.go`: **one line** (the import path). All used API exists in `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2/sparkline` v2.9.0: `New(w, h, opts...)`, `WithStyle(lipgloss.Style)` (lip gloss v2 type), `WithMaxValue`, `WithNoAutoMaxValue`, `PushAll`, `Draw`, `DrawBraille`, `Model.View() string`. Styles are `lipgloss.Style`, not a raw colour, so `color.Color` does not appear. The six chart tests (`TestEveryChartCellCarriesABackground`, `TestAChartLineIsExactlyTheColumnWidth`, …) pass.
134	
135	## 7. Rules 125 and 116, measure divergence
136	
137	Method: the same dump test run on `origin/main` (v1) and on the spike (v2), at 80x24, 120x40, 200x50, for (a) a datatable with an untitled `IconColumnWidth` (2) Nerd Font column (U+F07B, U+F0849, U+E725…) and rows holding VS16 emoji, flags, ZWJ, CJK, combining marks; (b) the viewer on a log with wide characters; (c) the setup wizard form. Per line: `ansi.StringWidth`, `runewidth.StringWidth` of the stripped text, and the text.
138	
139	- Layout (stripped text and `ansi.StringWidth` of every line): **identical v1 and v2 for the 9 dumps**. Table lines are all 78/118/198 cells (viewport minus the 2 border cells); Rule 116 holds, and `TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth` is green. Rule 125 holds: the icon column is 2 cells, glyph plus one cell, with no clipping.
140	- The only v1/v2 difference is the `runewidth` figure of lines containing a flag: 77 vs 78 (go-runewidth v0.0.16 to v0.0.31 now counts regional-indicator pairs as 2).
141	- `runewidth` vs the engine's measure (`ansi.StringWidth`, grapheme) vs `ansi.StringWidthWc` (per-rune wcwidth):
142	
143	| String | grapheme | wcwidth | runewidth v0.0.31 |
144	|---|---|---|---|
145	| `a❤️x` | 4 | 3 | 3 |
146	| `✔️`, `🛡️` | 2 | 1 | 1 |
147	| flag FR | 2 | 2 | 2 |
148	| ZWJ family | 2 | **6** | 2 |
149	| Nerd Font glyph (PUA) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
150	| CJK, `e`+U+0301 | 6 / 1 | 6 / 1 | 6 / 1 |
151	
152	  So `datatable`'s `runewidth` agrees with the grapheme measure except for VS16 emoji (3 vs 4), the case the Rule 116 test pins. **Not verifiable here:** which method the renderer uses. In bubbletea v2.1.1 the cell renderer starts in per-rune width and switches to `ansi.GraphemeWidth` only when the terminal answers the DECRQM query for mode 2027 (`tea.go` handling of `ModeReportMsg`). On a terminal without 2027 (support in Windows Terminal, tmux, Terminal.app not checked) a VS16 emoji or a ZWJ sequence would be laid out with another width than `datatable` assumes, shifting the rest of the line. Mitigation if it shows: keep emoji out of columns, or measure with `ansi.StringWidthWc` when mode 2027 is absent. Needs a real terminal test.
153	- 19 `runewidth.*` call sites in 3 production files remain (not 37/10: the rest are tests).
154	
155	## 8. Viewport and paste
156	
157	**Viewport.** Measured with `internal/app/spike_viewport_test.go`: a default v2 viewport scrolls horizontally on `right` (XOffset 6) and on `l`, and vertically on `j`. But only **one** viewport ever receives a raw key: the help overlay (`help_overlay.go:68`, `helpViewport.Update(msg)`), and it already installs `arrowOnlyScroll()`, whose `KeyMap` has no `Left`/`Right`. Test result: with that keymap, `left right h l j k space d u b f` leave X and Y at 0; `down` and `pgdown` still scroll. The other four viewports (app body, viewer, security and netdiag details) never get `Update`, they are driven with `SetYOffset`. So there is **nothing to disable**, contrary to the plan's "5 viewports". It is also not a v2 novelty: bubbles v0.21's `KeyMap` already has `Left`/`Right` (`left,h` / `right,l`), found in the module source. Keep the test, and the rule "a viewport that receives keys sets an explicit `KeyMap`".
158	
159	**Paste.** `tea.PasteMsg` does **not** reach the focused field by default: the router's `update` only switches on `tea.KeyMsg`. Four tests of DEVDESK-199 failed, as they were meant to: `TestPasteIntoCommandPaletteReachesTheField` (2 cases), `TestPasteWhileHelpIsOpenTriggersNothing`, and `TestTypedTextReachesTheFieldUnchanged/FilterBar`. Fixed in the spike:
160	- router: `case tea.PasteMsg: return a.handlePasteMsg(msg)`, 14 lines. Dropped during a context switch, help or context list; to `commandInput` in command mode; to the active view only when `inEditMode()`; else ignored. A paste can no longer fire `q`, `?` or `:` (Rule 111). `textinput` v2 turns newlines into spaces (`l1\nl2` gives `l1 l2`).
161	- `FilterBar.Update`: accept `tea.PasteMsg` next to `tea.KeyMsg`.
162	- **Still open**: 36 `msg.(tea.KeyMsg)` / `case tea.KeyMsg` gates in production code route text to inputs (30 files use `textinput` or `WrappedInput`). Every form or view with an edit mode must also accept `PasteMsg`. The existing paste tests cover the router, the palette, `FilterBar` and the components; the views' forms need one table-driven test each (add during S2).
163	
164	## 9. Conclusion: commit split and effort
165	
166	The ordering of the plan (§4, S2 a to g) is right. What the spike changes:
167	1. **The build cannot be compiled between commits anyway** (all of `charm.land/*/v2` at once), so the "commits" are review units, not bisect points; say so in the PR. Squashing is not advised, reviewers need the split.
168	2. Reordered and sized:
169	
170	| # | Commit | Content | Measured size |
171	|---|---|---|---|
172	| a | `theme` | `color.Color`, `contrast`/`tokencolors` via `RGBA()` + type check, `theme.Hex`, `StyleTextInput`, SGR reset literals | ~25 files |
173	| b | keys | `testutil` rewritten, `keymap.Space = "space"`, `tea.KeyMsg` to `tea.KeyPressMsg` (103 sites, optional but wanted), `source_guard_test` and `testutil` tests ported | ~10 files + the 103 sites |
174	| c | router | `Screen`, `Render`/`View` on 17 views + `App`, `AltScreen`, `.(Screen)` x14, `handlePasteMsg`, tests renamed to `Render()` | ~120 files, mostly scripted |
175	| d | bubbles | `textinput` `SetWidth` x23 and `SetStyles` x3, viewport options and accessors, `WithWhitespaceStyle` x16, paste in forms (36 gates), explicit `KeyMap` rule | ~60 files |
176	| e | ntcharts + ansi | import line, `go mod tidy` | 2 files |
177	| f | colour profile | `colorprofile` helper as no-op, drop `termenv`, `ansi.Strip` in the 7 tests, `main.go` `WithColorProfile` if `WT_SESSION` | ~15 files |
178	| g | docs | Rules 111 ("v1.3.10 does not enable"), 115 (cursor), 122, `app-shell.md`, `configuration.md`, `ui-components.md`; `TestNoPackageLevelVarRendersAString` comment | |
179	
180	3. Effort: L confirmed. The spike (mostly scripted) touched 209 production and 203 test files with about 100 lines of real logic (theme 4 spots, testutil 60 lines, router 15, `StyleTextInput` x3). Estimated 2 to 3 days to land cleanly (lint, `test-race`, review of the diff), plus half a day of manual checks.
181	
182	**Remaining risks and unknowns (not verified here):**
183	- Real terminals: mode 2027/2026 negotiation, WSL and Windows Terminal colours, Nerd Font rendering, tmux. Nothing was run in a TTY; only a captured `tea.Program` output.
184	- The four `tea.ExecProcess` sites (container shell `T`, OCI `-it`, pager `V`, workspace terminal): not exercised; API unchanged on paper.
185	- Visual check of the textinput virtual cursor background (Rule 115) and the footer filter bar.
186	- `TestMeasureRedrawCost` baseline not compared (the new renderer's cost is a claimed gain of the plan, not measured).
187	- `golangci-lint` and `test-race` not run on the spike.
188	- Silent `NoColor` on a bad theme hex (criterion 2); decide whether `ApplyTheme` validates.
189	- Router assertions `.(Screen)` (14) can panic at runtime; consider a typed `setView`.
190	- Paste in the 36 `KeyMsg`-gated views (criterion 8).
191	- `go-runewidth` moved to v0.0.31 through tidy, changing flag widths in the 19 remaining `runewidth` sites.
192	- `tea.KeyMsg` kept at 103 production sites matches key *release* events too; harmless until keyboard enhancements are requested, so migrate to `KeyPressMsg` in commit b.

# Spike DEVDESK-198: Charm v2 migration (Bubble Tea, Bubbles, Lip Gloss, ntcharts)

2026-11-10, Linux, Go 1.27.3. Base: `origin/main` at 63ebd72 (DEVDESK-197, 199, 200 merged).
Experiment code: branch `spike/charm-v2-code` (commit 217b389), **to be discarded, never merged**. This report is the only deliverable.
Pinned versions (not reopened): `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` v2.1.1, `charm.land/bubbles/v2` v2.2.1, `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` v2.0.6, `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` v0.11.9, `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` v2.9.0 (exact module path confirmed with `go list -m`; its `go.mod` requires bubbletea v2.1.1 and lipgloss v2.0.6, no `replace`). `go mod tidy` also pulled `go-runewidth` v0.0.16 to v0.0.31 and `colorprofile` v0.4.3.

Method: sed the imports, let the compiler lead, fix by category. The spike ended **with everything compiling and `go test ./...` green** (run once, `-timeout 100s`; `go vet ./...` clean). The only deleted tests are the three of `internal/ui/testutil` (`keys_test.go`, `source_guard_test.go`, `testutil_test.go`) and `colorprofile_test.go`, which test v1 APIs and are to be rewritten (see criteria 4 and 5). Not run: `mise run lint`, `test-race` (needs cgo), the app in a real terminal.

## Summary

| # | Criterion | Verdict | One line |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Imports on theme, datatable, about | OK | Mechanical. datatable: 0 production line beyond imports; theme: 4 logic spots; about: 1 method. The plan's counts hold, with two corrections (`termenv`, tests) |
| 2 | Palette `color.Color` | OK with reserve | 91 type sites, 3 logic spots; Rule 119 holds; **`lipgloss.Color("")` is `NoColor` whose `RGBA()` is opaque black** and an invalid hex is silently `NoColor` |
| 3 | `Render()` + `View() tea.View` + `Screen` | OK | Compiles, **0 `handle*` signature changed** (271 of them, 429 `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)` returns). Cost: 14 `.(Screen)` assertions in the router, tests renamed to `Render()` |
| 4 | Colour profile | OK with reserve | `tea.WithColorProfile` verified on a real `tea.Program`. 13 test files with termenv was really 3; **7 tests silently depended on the Ascii profile** |
| 5 | `testutil.Msgs` and `tea.Sequence` | OK | Reflection works unchanged: `sequenceMsg` is still `[]tea.Cmd` |
| 6 | ntcharts v2 sparkline | OK | One import line changed; `WithStyle(lipgloss.Style)` (v2); dashboard tests green |
| 7 | Rules 125 / 116, runewidth vs engine | OK with reserve | Layout byte-identical to v1 at 3 sizes. The engine's width depends on terminal mode 2027: **cannot be verified without a real terminal** |
| 8 | Viewport keys, `PasteMsg` | OK with reserve | Viewport: no change needed. **Paste is lost by the router and by every `KeyMsg`-gated field** (fixed in the router and `FilterBar`; ~34 sites remain to audit) |
| 9 | Commit split and effort | OK, adjusted | Same seven commits, reordered into compilable-in-the-end groups; effort L confirmed (2 to 3 days of coding, plus manual terminal checks) |

## 1. Imports on theme, datatable, about

Counts on `main` (import lines), against §1 of `charm-v2-impact.md`:

| Import | Plan | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| bubbletea | 239 files | 261 files (tests included) |
| lipgloss | 147 | 151 |
| bubbles spinner / textinput / table / viewport / key | 39 / 26 / 21 / 6 / 1 | 39 / 26 / 21 / 6 / 1 (identical) |
| x/ansi | 52 `ansi.*` | 53 imports |
| `termenv` | 13 test files | **3 files** (DEVDESK-199 funnelled it into `internal/testutil/colorprofile`; 50 callers of that helper stay unchanged) |

One `sed` over the whole repo (376 files) replaced them. Also needed: two `string`-literal fixes, because the sed hit import paths quoted in two guard tests.

What compiles and what breaks, per package, after the import swap only:

| Package | Production code | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `theme` | `colors.go`: 76 declarations `lipgloss.Color` to `color.Color` (type, mechanical). 15 more type sites elsewhere. `contrast.go`, `tokencolors.go` (read hex from the string): rewritten. `StyleTextInput` (textinput styles): rewritten. `manager.go`: **0 change** (`lipgloss.Color(hex)` is now a function and still compiles) | 72 compile errors in 13 files: 37 string constants given as `color.Color`, ~12 `string(c)`, 8 `lipgloss.TerminalColor`, rest `string` literals. Fixed with a 40-line script (wrap in `lipgloss.Color(...)`, `string(c)` to `theme.Hex(c)`). 1 failing test: the SGR reset is now `\x1b[m`, not `\x1b[0m` |
| `datatable` | **0 line** (builds as is, it does not use `bubbles/table` rendering) | compiles after `testutil` is ported; 4 tests fail until 8 literals `"\x1b[0m"` become `"\x1b[m"` |
| `about` | `View() string` becomes `Render() string` plus a 1-line `View() tea.View` | 3 `.View()` to `.Render()`; 1 test (see criterion 4) |
| `components` (dependency) | 2 sites `textinput.Width = n` to `SetWidth(n)` (23 such sites repo-wide) | 14 lines |

Whole repo, production code: 209 files, +747 / -623. Tests: 203 files, +1070 / -1585 (the deletions are the four removed test files). The compiler found everything except the five silent points listed in criteria 2, 4, 8 and below.

**Silent points actually hit** (compiler-silent, caught by tests): the space key (`keymap.Space` is `" "` in v1; flipping that one constant to `"space"` took the failures from about 50 to 11, which is the DEVDESK-200 payoff); the paste (criterion 8); the SGR reset `\x1b[m` (9 literals in 6 test files: 8 in datatable, 1 regexp in theme; `overlay.go` already accepts both); 7 tests that assumed no ANSI (criterion 4).

Mechanical changes beyond imports, with site counts: `WithWhitespaceBackground` to `WithWhitespaceStyle(NewStyle().Background(c))` 16 sites (exact match with the plan); `textinput` `.Width` 23; textinput style assignments 3 (`theme.StyleTextInput`, `setup/styles.go`, `paletteInputView`); viewport `New(w,h)` 4, `.Width/.Height/.YOffset` reads and writes about 50 (including tests); `tea.WithAltScreen` 2 (now `View.AltScreen`). `bubbles/table` and `spinner` needed **no** change. `tea.KeyMsg` stays compilable (it is now an interface matching press and release): 103 production sites still use it; it works but should become `tea.KeyPressMsg` (release events only exist with keyboard enhancements, which we do not request).

## 2. Palette

Port (what I did): every `var Color… lipgloss.Color` becomes `color.Color` (`import "image/color"`). Semantic aliases (`ColorTableLineSelected`, `ColorSyntax*`, `ColorFooter*`, `IconColor`, `TokenColor`, `indicator.Color`, `cmdsuggest.Fg/Bg`) carry the same `color.Color`; an alias is an assignment, so `ApplyTheme` is unchanged.

**Rule 119** (hex only in `colors.go`): holds. `colors.go` only declares; the hex strings live in `manager.go`'s `DefaultTheme` and theme files, and `ApplyTheme` calls `lipgloss.Color(hexString)` exactly as before. A grep for `#rrggbb` literals outside `manager.go`/`colors.go` finds comments only. The one addition is `theme.Hex(c color.Color) string` (formats `#rrggbb` or `none`), used by tests in place of `string(c)`; it produces hex, it does not hold any.

`contrast.go` reads components through `RGBA()` (`uint32`, 16-bit, shift by 8), after a type check:

```go
if _, ok := c.(color.RGBA); !ok { return error }   // only "#rgb"/"#rrggbb" come out as color.RGBA
r, g, b, _ := c.RGBA()
```

Without the type check the old contract ("hex only, else error") is lost, because of the empty-colour semantics below. `TestContrast*`, `ColorDistance` pass; their "error" table (`"", "red", "12", "ffffff", "#ggg"...`) still errors, now because those values become `NoColor` or `ansi.BasicColor`.

**Empty colour** (`iconcolors.go`, measured):

| Input | v2 type | `RGBA()` | `Render` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lipgloss.Color("")` | `lipgloss.NoColor` | **0 0 0 65535 (opaque black)** | no SGR emitted ("inherits", same effect as v1) |
| `Color("red")`, `Color("#ggg")` | `NoColor` (silently) | opaque black | none |
| `Color("#fff")` | `color.RGBA` | ok | 38;2 |
| `Color("12")` | `ansi.BasicColor` | palette | 38;5/ANSI |
| `NewStyle().GetForeground()` (unset) | `NoColor{}`, `== Color("")` is true | | |

Consequences: (a) the rendering semantics of "no colour" are preserved, so the `IconColor` rule (unknown role falls back to `ColorText`, never the zero Color) still protects Rule 122 and `IconColor("nope") == ColorText` passes; (b) **anything reading components must type-check first**, because `NoColor.RGBA()` is black; (c) `app_header.go:190` (`GetForeground() != lipgloss.Color("")`) keeps working through interface equality; (d) **a typo in a theme hex is now silently no colour**, where `lipgloss.Color` kept the string; if `ApplyTheme` should reject it, validate at load (not done in the spike, flagged as a risk). Reserve: the `textinput` virtual cursor style is `NewStyle().Foreground(Cursor.Color)` only, so the cursor cell loses the old `Background(ColorBackground)` (Rule 115); visual check needed.

## 3. Architecture: `Render() string` + `View() tea.View` + `Screen`

Done as decided:

```go
// each of the 17 views
func (m Model) Render() string { ... }                         // was View() string
func (m Model) View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }

// router
type Screen interface { tea.Model; Render() string }
views map[command.ViewType]Screen
func (a *App) View() tea.View { v := tea.NewView(a.Render()); v.AltScreen = true; return v }
```

`main.go` loses `tea.WithAltScreen()`; the setup wizard (its own root program) sets `AltScreen` in its own `View`.

Result: **compiles, and no `handle*` signature changed.** `grep` finds 271 `handle*(...) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)` and 429 `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)` returns in production code (the plan said ~480); the diff touches none of them (the only added one is `handlePasteMsg`). Reason: `tea.Model` is still satisfied by the view.

What it costs:
- 17 views: 17 renames + 17 one-line wrappers (scripted).
- Router: `Update` of a view returns `tea.Model`, so every `a.views[x] = updated` needs `updated.(Screen)`: **14 sites** in `internal/app` (it panics if a view stops implementing `Render`). A helper `a.setView(name, tea.Model)` would centralise it; I did not.
- 5 fake views in `internal/app/*_test.go` (+2 program wrappers): rename plus wrapper; `router()`, `routerAt()`, `commanding()` take a `Screen`.
- Tests: `.View()` on a view model becomes `.Render()`. 450 `.View()` calls in 104 test files; a script renamed all in the 17 view packages and `internal/app`, then reverted the 115 that were components (`datatable`, `FilterBar`, forms, which keep `View() string`). Tests may equally call `View().Content` (a `string` field, set by `NewView`); `Render()` is shorter and does not allocate a `tea.View`. Recommendation: `Render()` in tests.
- Components (`datatable`, `components.*`, `status/components`) keep `View() string`, as planned. Guards keyed on the method name `View` do not exist (`grep '"View"'` finds one test map), so the AST guards (`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody`, footer guards) are unaffected by the rename.

## 4. Colour profile

`lipgloss.SetColorProfile` is gone; `Style.Render` now always emits full colour (`\x1b[38;2;r;g;bm`). `internal/testutil/colorprofile` therefore keeps its API (`TrueColor(t)`, `Force()`) as **no-ops** (50 callers untouched) and its own test file is deleted; `termenv` leaves `go.mod`. `source_guard_test.go` still needs the same rule re-aimed ("no import of `colorprofile` other than the helper, no hand-built `tea.KeyPressMsg{}`").

Replacement validated on a real `tea.Program` (`internal/app/spike_profile_test.go`, 3 cases, output captured in a buffer):

| `tea.WithColorProfile(...)` | `38;2;` | `38;5;` | `38;` | alt screen `\x1b[?1049h` | bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TrueColor | yes | | | yes | 3499 |
| ANSI256 | no | yes | | yes | 2634 |
| Ascii | no | no | no | yes | 1402 |

So downsampling happens at the output, and `View.AltScreen` replaces the program option. `ColorProfileMsg` is sent by the program after capability detection; the `main.go` `COLORTERM`/`WT_SESSION` workaround can become `tea.WithColorProfile(colorprofile.TrueColor)` when `WT_SESSION` is set (not changed in the spike; WSL/Windows Terminal not verified).

Guards:
- `TestNoViewStylesItsOwnFooterMessage`: AST scan of function names containing `RenderFooter`/`InfoLine`/`InfoText`; passes unchanged, keeps its meaning.
- `TestNoPackageLevelVarRendersAString`: passes unchanged. Its doc comment lists two causes; **cause 2 (lipgloss `sync.Once` locking the profile at init) no longer exists**, cause 1 (string frozen on the default theme) remains and is enough to keep the test. Update the comment.
- datatable tests: all pass after the eight `\x1b[0m` literals. The Rule 116 tests (`TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth`) pass with x/ansi v0.11.9.
- **Hidden dependency found**: 7 tests asserted "blank line" or "empty info line" on raw `Render()` output and passed only because `go test` had no TTY, hence the Ascii profile (`about_test.go` says so in a comment: "under `go test` lipgloss finds no TTY and emits none"). In v2 the same line is `ESC[38;2;…m   ESC[m`. Fixed with `ansi.Strip` in `about`, `configuration`, `dashboard`, `netdiag`, `oci_resources`, `security` (x2). These tests did not check what they claimed to; `ansi.Strip` is the right form.

## 5. `testutil.Msgs` and `tea.Sequence`

Works unchanged. bubbletea v2.1.1 still has `type sequenceMsg []Cmd` (unexported) and `type BatchMsg []Cmd` (exported); the reflection (`Kind()==Slice && Elem()==TypeFor[tea.Cmd]()`) matches as before. Tested: `Msgs(tea.Sequence(c(1), tea.Batch(c(2), c(3)), c(4)))` returns the four messages in order. No replacement needed. Risk to note: this relies on the type staying a `[]Cmd`; `internal/ui/testutil` should keep the test that fails if bubbletea changes it.

Other `testutil` changes (one 60-line file rewritten, all of `Key`/`Type`/`Paste`/`IsText`/`Text`): `Key` returns `tea.KeyPressMsg{Code, Text, Mod}`; space is `{Code: KeySpace, Text: " "}` (its `String()` is `"space"`); `alt+x` must clear `Text` (otherwise `String()` returns `x`, found by a test); `shift+tab` is `{Code: KeyTab, Mod: ModShift}`; `Paste` is `tea.PasteMsg{Content}`. The 1295 `testutil.Key` call sites needed no change; 22 tests that name `tea.KeyMsg` kept compiling.

## 6. ntcharts v2 sparkline

OK. `internal/ui/dashboard/chart.go`: **one line** (the import path). All used API exists in `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2/sparkline` v2.9.0: `New(w, h, opts...)`, `WithStyle(lipgloss.Style)` (lip gloss v2 type), `WithMaxValue`, `WithNoAutoMaxValue`, `PushAll`, `Draw`, `DrawBraille`, `Model.View() string`. Styles are `lipgloss.Style`, not a raw colour, so `color.Color` does not appear. The six chart tests (`TestEveryChartCellCarriesABackground`, `TestAChartLineIsExactlyTheColumnWidth`, …) pass.

## 7. Rules 125 and 116, measure divergence

Method: the same dump test run on `origin/main` (v1) and on the spike (v2), at 80x24, 120x40, 200x50, for (a) a datatable with an untitled `IconColumnWidth` (2) Nerd Font column (U+F07B, U+F0849, U+E725…) and rows holding VS16 emoji, flags, ZWJ, CJK, combining marks; (b) the viewer on a log with wide characters; (c) the setup wizard form. Per line: `ansi.StringWidth`, `runewidth.StringWidth` of the stripped text, and the text.

- Layout (stripped text and `ansi.StringWidth` of every line): **identical v1 and v2 for the 9 dumps**. Table lines are all 78/118/198 cells (viewport minus the 2 border cells); Rule 116 holds, and `TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth` is green. Rule 125 holds: the icon column is 2 cells, glyph plus one cell, with no clipping.
- The only v1/v2 difference is the `runewidth` figure of lines containing a flag: 77 vs 78 (go-runewidth v0.0.16 to v0.0.31 now counts regional-indicator pairs as 2).
- `runewidth` vs the engine's measure (`ansi.StringWidth`, grapheme) vs `ansi.StringWidthWc` (per-rune wcwidth):

| String | grapheme | wcwidth | runewidth v0.0.31 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a❤️x` | 4 | 3 | 3 |
| `✔️`, `🛡️` | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| flag FR | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| ZWJ family | 2 | **6** | 2 |
| Nerd Font glyph (PUA) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| CJK, `e`+U+0301 | 6 / 1 | 6 / 1 | 6 / 1 |

  So `datatable`'s `runewidth` agrees with the grapheme measure except for VS16 emoji (3 vs 4), the case the Rule 116 test pins. **Not verifiable here:** which method the renderer uses. In bubbletea v2.1.1 the cell renderer starts in per-rune width and switches to `ansi.GraphemeWidth` only when the terminal answers the DECRQM query for mode 2027 (`tea.go` handling of `ModeReportMsg`). On a terminal without 2027 (support in Windows Terminal, tmux, Terminal.app not checked) a VS16 emoji or a ZWJ sequence would be laid out with another width than `datatable` assumes, shifting the rest of the line. Mitigation if it shows: keep emoji out of columns, or measure with `ansi.StringWidthWc` when mode 2027 is absent. Needs a real terminal test.
- 19 `runewidth.*` call sites in 3 production files remain (not 37/10: the rest are tests).

## 8. Viewport and paste

**Viewport.** Measured with `internal/app/spike_viewport_test.go`: a default v2 viewport scrolls horizontally on `right` (XOffset 6) and on `l`, and vertically on `j`. But only **one** viewport ever receives a raw key: the help overlay (`help_overlay.go:68`, `helpViewport.Update(msg)`), and it already installs `arrowOnlyScroll()`, whose `KeyMap` has no `Left`/`Right`. Test result: with that keymap, `left right h l j k space d u b f` leave X and Y at 0; `down` and `pgdown` still scroll. The other four viewports (app body, viewer, security and netdiag details) never get `Update`, they are driven with `SetYOffset`. So there is **nothing to disable**, contrary to the plan's "5 viewports". It is also not a v2 novelty: bubbles v0.21's `KeyMap` already has `Left`/`Right` (`left,h` / `right,l`), found in the module source. Keep the test, and the rule "a viewport that receives keys sets an explicit `KeyMap`".

**Paste.** `tea.PasteMsg` does **not** reach the focused field by default: the router's `update` only switches on `tea.KeyMsg`. Four tests of DEVDESK-199 failed, as they were meant to: `TestPasteIntoCommandPaletteReachesTheField` (2 cases), `TestPasteWhileHelpIsOpenTriggersNothing`, and `TestTypedTextReachesTheFieldUnchanged/FilterBar`. Fixed in the spike:
- router: `case tea.PasteMsg: return a.handlePasteMsg(msg)`, 14 lines. Dropped during a context switch, help or context list; to `commandInput` in command mode; to the active view only when `inEditMode()`; else ignored. A paste can no longer fire `q`, `?` or `:` (Rule 111). `textinput` v2 turns newlines into spaces (`l1\nl2` gives `l1 l2`).
- `FilterBar.Update`: accept `tea.PasteMsg` next to `tea.KeyMsg`.
- **Still open**: 36 `msg.(tea.KeyMsg)` / `case tea.KeyMsg` gates in production code route text to inputs (30 files use `textinput` or `WrappedInput`). Every form or view with an edit mode must also accept `PasteMsg`. The existing paste tests cover the router, the palette, `FilterBar` and the components; the views' forms need one table-driven test each (add during S2).

## 9. Conclusion: commit split and effort

The ordering of the plan (§4, S2 a to g) is right. What the spike changes:
1. **The build cannot be compiled between commits anyway** (all of `charm.land/*/v2` at once), so the "commits" are review units, not bisect points; say so in the PR. Squashing is not advised, reviewers need the split.
2. Reordered and sized:

| # | Commit | Content | Measured size |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | `theme` | `color.Color`, `contrast`/`tokencolors` via `RGBA()` + type check, `theme.Hex`, `StyleTextInput`, SGR reset literals | ~25 files |
| b | keys | `testutil` rewritten, `keymap.Space = "space"`, `tea.KeyMsg` to `tea.KeyPressMsg` (103 sites, optional but wanted), `source_guard_test` and `testutil` tests ported | ~10 files + the 103 sites |
| c | router | `Screen`, `Render`/`View` on 17 views + `App`, `AltScreen`, `.(Screen)` x14, `handlePasteMsg`, tests renamed to `Render()` | ~120 files, mostly scripted |
| d | bubbles | `textinput` `SetWidth` x23 and `SetStyles` x3, viewport options and accessors, `WithWhitespaceStyle` x16, paste in forms (36 gates), explicit `KeyMap` rule | ~60 files |
| e | ntcharts + ansi | import line, `go mod tidy` | 2 files |
| f | colour profile | `colorprofile` helper as no-op, drop `termenv`, `ansi.Strip` in the 7 tests, `main.go` `WithColorProfile` if `WT_SESSION` | ~15 files |
| g | docs | Rules 111 ("v1.3.10 does not enable"), 115 (cursor), 122, `app-shell.md`, `configuration.md`, `ui-components.md`; `TestNoPackageLevelVarRendersAString` comment | |

3. Effort: L confirmed. The spike (mostly scripted) touched 209 production and 203 test files with about 100 lines of real logic (theme 4 spots, testutil 60 lines, router 15, `StyleTextInput` x3). Estimated 2 to 3 days to land cleanly (lint, `test-race`, review of the diff), plus half a day of manual checks.

**Remaining risks and unknowns (not verified here):**
- Real terminals: mode 2027/2026 negotiation, WSL and Windows Terminal colours, Nerd Font rendering, tmux. Nothing was run in a TTY; only a captured `tea.Program` output.
- The four `tea.ExecProcess` sites (container shell `T`, OCI `-it`, pager `V`, workspace terminal): not exercised; API unchanged on paper.
- Visual check of the textinput virtual cursor background (Rule 115) and the footer filter bar.
- `TestMeasureRedrawCost` baseline not compared (the new renderer's cost is a claimed gain of the plan, not measured).
- `golangci-lint` and `test-race` not run on the spike.
- Silent `NoColor` on a bad theme hex (criterion 2); decide whether `ApplyTheme` validates.
- Router assertions `.(Screen)` (14) can panic at runtime; consider a typed `setView`.
- Paste in the 36 `KeyMsg`-gated views (criterion 8).
- `go-runewidth` moved to v0.0.31 through tidy, changing flag widths in the 19 remaining `runewidth` sites.
- `tea.KeyMsg` kept at 103 production sites matches key *release* events too; harmless until keyboard enhancements are requested, so migrate to `KeyPressMsg` in commit b.

En tant que mainteneur, je veux un spike borné (1 à 2 jours, aucun code mergé) qui tente la migration sur une branche jetable afin de lever les inconnues et de confirmer le plan de la PR atomique (story de migration) avant d'engager le gros du travail.

Critères d'acceptation

  • Given une branche jetable sous .worktrees/ et les versions cibles fixées (bubbletea v2.1.1, bubbles v2.2.1, lipgloss v2.0.6, x/ansi v0.11.9, ntcharts/v2 v2.9.0) When le spike remplace les imports par charm.land/*/v2 sur theme, datatable et une vue témoin (about) Then un rapport liste ce qui compile, ce qui casse et le nombre de sites à changer par catégorie, à comparer au tableau de .claude/plans/charm-v2-impact.md (§1).

  • Given l'architecture décidée (chaque vue garde Render() string et expose View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) } ; interface Screen dans le routeur ; le routeur seul fixe l'état du terminal) When elle est essayée sur le routeur et deux vues (about, une vue à tableau) Then le spike confirme qu'elle compile avec les signatures handle* inchangées (Rule 201, environ 480) et que les tests peuvent appeler Render() ou View().Content.

  • Given lipgloss v2 qui supprime SetColorProfile (13 fichiers de test avec termenv) When les tests qui comparent de l'ANSI sont portés Then le spike valide le remplacement (profil géré par Bubble Tea : ColorProfileMsg, tea.WithColorProfile) et vérifie que TestNoViewStylesItsOwnFooterMessage, les tests de datatable et TestNoPackageLevelVarRendersAString gardent leur sens.

  • Given testutil.Msgs, qui déplie tea.Sequence par réflexion sur un type non exporté When il tourne sous bubbletea v2 Then le spike confirme que cela marche encore, ou propose un remplacement.

  • Given ntcharts/v2 v2.9.0 (go 1.26.8) When le sparkline du dashboard (internal/ui/dashboard/chart.go) est porté Then le spike confirme que l'API utilisée existe en v2 et que ses styles prennent un color.Color.

  • Given x/ansi 0.11.9 et le moteur de rendu v2 (largeur Unicode, mode 2027) When trois écrans de référence (tableau avec colonne d'icônes Nerd Font, viewer, formulaire) sont rendus avant et après à trois tailles de terminal Then le spike dit si la Rule 125 (colonne d'icônes, IconColumnWidth 2) et la Rule 116 (largeur exacte, RenderedWidth) tiennent, et si la mesure runewidth de datatable diverge de celle du moteur.

  • Given un viewport v2 et un champ de saisie When le spike les essaie Then il confirme que ←/→ défilent par défaut dans le viewport (à désactiver, Rule 135) et que tea.PasteMsg arrive au champ focalisé.

  • Given le résultat When le spike conclut Then il confirme ou ajuste le découpage en commits ordonnés de la story de migration atomique (thème, touches, routeur, bubbles, ntcharts, profil couleur, docs) et son effort ; il ne rouvre pas le choix des versions (décidé).

Contexte

Effort : M. Dépendances : après DEVDESK-197 (Go ≥ 1.26.8 requis). Le guide bubbletea ne couvre que Bubble Tea ; lipgloss et bubbles ont leurs propres UPGRADE_GUIDE_V2.md. Livrable : un rapport (commentaire Plane ou docs/product/charm-v2/), pas de code mergé. Décision de l'utilisateur (2026-11-09) : la migration est atomique, en une seule PR, et non plus en 6 lots sur une branche charm-v2 ; le spike sert à la sécuriser. Module : Migration Go 1.27 et Charm v2.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` is strict: an unknown name panics. The
space key is built as a key (`KeySpace` + rune `' '`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). The colour profile is forced through
`internal/testutil/colorprofile` (`TrueColor(t)`, `Force()` in `TestMain`), the only
importer of termenv; it is a leaf package because testutil→shortcut→theme would
cycle. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a hand-built
key, a termenv import or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Two guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`) fail the
suite otherwise; limits are listed in `docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` is strict: an unknown name panics. The
space key is built as a key (`KeySpace` + rune `' '`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). The colour profile is forced through
`internal/testutil/colorprofile` (`TrueColor(t)`, `Force()` in `TestMain`), the only
importer of termenv; it is a leaf package because testutil→shortcut→theme would
cycle. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a hand-built
key, a termenv import or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Two guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`) fail the
suite otherwise; limits are listed in `docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

</system-reminder>
